content.title: About
content.content: Turkey is a tender, lean poultry meat rich in high‑quality protein, B‑vitamins, and essential minerals. For toddlers it provides a valuable source of energy and supports proper muscle and nervous system development. It is usually served as a puree or finely shredded pieces, prepared without added salt or strong spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey contains less fat than chicken and virtually no cholesterol.
It is high in tryptophan, an amino acid involved in serotonin production, which may help promote a good mood.
Turkey is considered a "gentle" meat and is often introduced to babies after 6–12 months of age.
Unlike red meat, turkey provides non‑heme iron that is easily absorbed when paired with vitamin‑C‑rich vegetables.

items.title: Rich in high‑quality protein
items.content: Easily digestible protein supports the growth of muscle tissue in young children.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey supplies vitamin B6 and niacin (B3), which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: Contains phosphorus, selenium and zinc – key for bone health, immune function and hormonal balance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Its leanness helps keep the overall calorie density of a toddler’s diet moderate.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Selenium provides antioxidant protection for cells.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some children may develop an allergic reaction to poultry; introduce gradually and monitor for symptoms.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Turkey must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate salmonella and campylobacter.

items.title: Texture
items.content: For infants under 12 months the meat should be pureed to avoid choking hazards.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Do not add salt, as a toddler’s kidneys are not yet efficient at excreting sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steam, boil or bake turkey without added fat, then blend into a smooth puree. You can mix in a small amount of vegetable puree (e.g., carrot or pumpkin) for flavor and extra nutrients. For older toddlers, serve finely shredded pieces mixed into cereal or rice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared puree in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 1 month. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature.
